subject: Cross-border handoffs and evidence playbook for inference processing
messages:
From: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@medicore.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai, legal@medicore.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Inquiry: where inference requests are executed + subprocessor chain for procurement

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for taking our call earlier. As part of Medicore's procurement checklist we need a concise, procurement-ready answer to a few technical/data-residency items. Can you confirm:

- Which regions (cloud regions / POPs) handle inference for the hosted Redwood API by default? Do requests ever leave a customer-designated region?
- Full list of subprocessors involved in request handling (compute, autoscaling, monitoring, logging, storage) and the countries where those subprocessors operate.
- For cross-border transfers, what legal mechanisms do you rely on (SCCs, BCRs, standard contractual clauses, or customer-specific addenda)?
- Retention/deletion guarantees: once our customer data is deleted from our account, how long before it is removed from caches, backups, logs, and analytics? Any SLA we can cite?
- If we need strict EU-only processing, what are our options (dedicated region pinning, private deployment, on-prem)?

Procurement needs a short evidence pack to attach to the SOW; any artifacts (subprocessor map, regional processing diagram, deletion flow) would be helpful.

If easier, please point me to a drive folder or we can schedule a 30-min tech walk.

Appreciate it —
Sanjay Patel
Head of IT Procurement
Medicore Health

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@medicore.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: where inference requests are executed + subprocessor chain for procurement

Hi Sanjay —

Thanks for the clear list. Short version up front, full details and attachments below. I put Ben (account lead) and Laura (security) on copy for technical artifacts and legal language.

High-level:
- Default processing regions: US (primary: us-east1, us-west2) and EU (eu-west1) for the hosted API. Live requests are routed to the nearest healthy POP by default.
- Cross-border transfers: transient request metadata or KV cache entries may touch other regions for routing/failover; we do not persist raw customer content outside the region unless customer chooses a non-regional deployment.
- Subprocessors: compute (AWS/GCP/Azure by region), metrics & logging (Datadog), error-tracking (Sentry), observability storage (BigQuery / Snowflake depending on customer region), and CDNs for streaming. See attached Subprocessor_Chain_Map_20260914.csv.
- Legal controls: we use SCCs where applicable and offer contract language addenda for EU processing; Dedicated and Private deployments provide region pinning and eliminate cross-region routing for inference.
- Retention & deletion: customer-managed deletion triggers an internal erase workflow — ephemeral cache entries are invalidated immediately; primary session logs and telemetry are deleted within 30 days unless retained for compliance or opt-in analytics. We provide a 30-day deletion SLA for hosted accounts (shorter windows possible for Dedicated/Private). Laura added more below.

Attachments included: Regional_Processing_Summary_v1.pdf (diagram + narrative), Subprocessor_Chain_Map_20260914.csv (names, countries, roles). Evidence folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/abc123-evidence-pkg

Next steps I suggest: 1) Laura to confirm exact legal controls and deletion SLA language for your SOW, 2) Ben to book a 30-min tech walk to show the processing map and where we can pin region, 3) we drop the evidence pack into your procurement folder.

Do any of those work?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Sanjay Patel <sanjay@medicore.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Inquiry: where inference requests are executed + subprocessor chain for procurement

Hi Sanjay —

Adding the security/compliance specifics you asked for so procurement has precise language to include in the SOW. See the bullets below and feel free to quote them directly.

Encryption & key management:
- Data in transit: TLS 1.2+ for all API and internal service traffic.
- Data at rest: customer data stored in region is encrypted with AES-256.
- KMS: For hosted customers we manage keys via cloud KMS; Dedicated and Private deployments support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) and can be configured with bring-your-own-key (BYOK).

Subprocessor locations & responsibilities (summary):
- Compute: AWS (us-east1/us-west2), GCP (eu-west1), Azure (apac where applicable).
- Metrics & Logs: Datadog (US/EU endpoints), long-term analytics (BigQuery/Snowflake depending on customer region).
- Observability/Tracing: Sentry (operational metadata only; we scrub PII per our ingestion filters).
- Backup & Disaster Recovery: encrypted snapshots retained only for up to 30 days in hosted mode; Dedicated/Private can alter retention windows by contract.

Cross-border transfer mechanics:
- We rely on EU SCCs for transfers originating in the EU in hosted contexts.
- For customers requiring strict EU processing we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity pinned to eu-west1) or Private (VPC/on-prem) — both options remove the need for SCCs by keeping processing in-circumscribed boundaries.

Deletion & evidence:
- Deletion workflow: 1) immediate user-visible deletion, 2) invalidate caches and remove active KV entries within minutes, 3) purge logs/analytics and snapshots within 30 days; cryptographic erasure on keys occurs within 72 hours for scoped retention expiries where applicable.
- Audit evidence: we can provide time-stamped logs showing deletion initiation and finalization for the account, and a subprocessor attestations list for procurement.
- SLA language: hosted customers get a standard 30-day deletion window in the contract; we can add a contract clause for faster deletion timelines for Dedicated/Private customers.

Compliance posture & artifacts available: SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), vendor/subprocessor roster, processing location diagrams, and sample deletion logs. We can assemble a procurement-ready zip with those items.

If you want exact clause text for SCCs or a draft addendum for region pinning, I can share sample language for your legal team.

Regards,
Laura Bennett
Security & Compliance Lead | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai
